subject: Re: Competitive eval — model quality follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next tests from today's competitive eval call

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Recap from today
- You ran our initial quality pass against your 200-shot internal prompt set (mixed support tickets + product FAQs).
- We saw preliminary differences vs Hyperscaler A (Bedrock) and Hyperscaler B (Vertex): Redwood model had lower hallucination rate on entity extraction tests and stronger grounding on FAQ-style completions.
- Latency looked comparable in the hosted test (p95 ~220ms token rate for the short prompts), but you flagged long-context regressions on multi-paragraph summarization.

What we propose next
1) Regression checks: run the same 200-shot set with longer context windows (8k tokens) and measure hallucination delta and factuality scores.
2) Adversarial prompts: run our adversarial suite (edge-case entity swaps) to quantify hallucination and safety gating.
3) Production-like throughput: we offer to run a Dedicated latency pass with your approximate QPS to validate p95/p99 under batching/kv-cache.
4) Share canonical eval prompts and expected outputs (attached eval_prompts_v1.txt). Please add any domain-specific cases you want included.

Quick numbers (prelim) — from the call:
- Hallucination (entity hallucinations on extraction tasks): Redwood 3.8% vs Hyperscaler A 7.2% vs Hyperscaler B 6.9%
- Factuality (automated QA metric): Redwood 89.3 vs Hyperscaler A 83.7
- Short-prompt p95 latency: Redwood hosted ~220ms, Hyperscaler A ~210ms (similar), Hyperscaler B ~240ms

Attachments: eval_prompts_v1.txt (list of prompts + expected checks). I'll upload a CSV with the first-pass results once the batch finishes (targeting Wed morning PST).

Ask: Can you confirm (1) which additional domain docs we should include, and (2) whether we should schedule a Dedicated-run for Wednesday afternoon? If yes, we'll coordinate with Aditya for capacity and Neha for the evaluation harness.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0103

[Attachment: eval_prompts_v1.txt]

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeanalytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next tests from today's competitive eval call

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Domain docs: please include the support KB (support-kb_v2.pdf) and our product glossary (prod-glossary_v1.csv).
2) We'd like the adversarial suite to emphasize entity-preservation (product codes, customer names) — last time Bedrock swapped product codes in ~5% of cases which caused bad downstream routing.
3) For Dedicated-run timing: Wednesday afternoon (PST) works for us, but we need to confirm a 2 hour window to simulate spikes. Can you also share the expected p99 latency under Dedicated? Our internal SLO target is <=600ms p99 for 8k token contexts.

Also, can you share the initial CSV once you have it so our SREs can start looking at diffs?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of ML Ops | Acme Analytics
sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com

[External note: attaching support-kb_v2.pdf via separate upload]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next tests from today's competitive eval call

Sara / Tom —

Attached: acme_eval_results_v1.csv (first-pass results) and a draft mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf). High level summary below.

Summary of first-pass results (attached CSV has line-level metrics)
- Hallucination (entity extraction): Redwood 3.8% (31/820), Hyperscaler A 7.2% (59/820), Hyperscaler B 6.9% (57/820).
- Long-context summarization (8k subset, 120 examples): Redwood factuality score 86.1 vs Hyperscaler A 79.4. We still see a small number of "context drop" regressions when the prompt contains 3+ embedded tables.
- Safety/adversarial: on the initial adversarial suite (50 cases), Redwood failed 2 cases where product-code formatting confused the parser; Hyperscaler A failed 6.
- Latency (hosted, short prompts): p95 ~220ms; Dedicated estimates (based on earlier runs with identical instance types) p95 ~160ms, p99 ~450ms for 8k contexts with batching enabled — we'll confirm during the Dedicated-run.

Next tests we recommend (and timeline)
- Wed 5 Aug, 14:00-16:00 PST: Dedicated throughput + p99 validation (we'll provision a reserved pool for the 2 hrs). Aditya — can you confirm capacity and the instance types?
- Thu 6 Aug: expanded adversarial sweep (200 cases) including product-code permutations and named-entity swaps. Neha — can you run the extended QA harness and push diffs to the Drive folder?
- After the Dedicated-run we'll produce an updated CSV with per-prompt diffs and a small report on hallucination root causes (aim Fri EOD).

Attachments: acme_eval_results_v1.csv (first-pass), mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf (draft MAP).

Let me know if you want us to include any additional model variants (lower-quant, 4-bit) in the Dedicated run — we can test a quantized variant to show cost/quality tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Marissa

[Attachment: acme_eval_results_v1.csv] [Attachment: mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Acme Dedicated-run + extended eval (Wed/Thu)

Aditya / Neha —

Looping you both in officially from the customer thread above. TL;DR: Acme wants a 2 hour Dedicated-run today 14:00-16:00 PST to validate p99 for 8k contexts and then an expanded adversarial sweep tomorrow.

Aditya: can you confirm capacity (instance types + pool size) and post the reservation here? They asked for p99 <=600ms target; our prior runs show p99 ~450ms for the same instance class but please verify.

Neha: please queue the extended 200-case adversarial suite and push results to the Drive folder referenced in the thread. Use the attached eval_prompts_v1.txt and add the product-code permutations Sara called out. Start the run after the Dedicated window so we can compare under load.

I'll take point on communicating the CSV/report back to Sara and Tom. Please keep me looped if you hit any unexpected regressions.

-Marissa
